findings.title: Two keybind descriptions leak M200 milestone ID
findings.description: 46-description table includes two entries referencing M200 by ID, violating AC-04: (1) keybinds.focus_content description contains "after M200 — see M200 release note"; (2) keybinds.refresh description contains "Default changed in M200 from r to Ctrl-R". Both rendered to end users via `mp config schema`. Rewrite without the milestone ID.
findings.resolution: Fixed: the two keybind descriptions (keybinds.focus_content and keybinds.refresh) no longer reference M200 or the project changelog. The 46-description table was re-baked into the spec's scope.in_scope delimiter-wrapped block. Verified: zero M-digit matches across all 46 descriptions.

findings.title: No version pin or fallback when raul reads `mp config schema` from an older mp
findings.description: The Settings 2.0 lane reads the schema on lane open via `mp config schema`. If a user upgrades raul (M201) without upgrading mp, the schema subcommand does not exist on the older mp, and the lane fails to load (no fallback). The spec should either: (a) require a minimum mp version and surface a clear error in the Settings lane if the installed mp is too old; or (b) ship a fallback JSON schema in the raul binary that is used if `mp config schema` is unavailable. Pick (a) — simpler, and the upgrade coupling is already implicit because the renderer also reads `mp config get` / `mp config set` paths. State the minimum mp version in the design decisions and add an AC for the version-check error path.
findings.target: scope.in_scope (Settings schema cache) / design_decisions["Schema fetch on lane open"]
findings.resolution: Fixed: new design decision ('Minimum mp version for Settings 2.0') added. New AC-08 covers the version-check error path. New step S16 under WP4 adds the TUI test. Note: the actual minimum mp version is left as 0.X.Y; the executor replaces X.Y when the mp version that ships mp config schema is finalized.

findings.title: Schema output format has no explicit version field for forward compat
findings.description: `mp config schema` emits a JSON document that raul parses on lane open. The spec describes the per-entry shape (`{key, type, default, allowed?, description}`) but does not include a top-level version field. A future schema change (added fields, renamed fields) would silently break consumers that do strict shape checks. Add a top-level `$schema_version: 1` (or `version: 1`) field to the output and document the forward-compat contract: additive changes bump minor, breaking changes bump major. Mention this in AC-01 (the schema output is a stable contract).
findings.resolution: Fixed: AC-01 updated to require a top-level $schema_version: 1 field. New design decision ('Schema output versioning') added with the forward-compat contract: additive changes bump minor, breaking changes bump major (semver). The exact initial version is left as 1.0; the executor picks the value but the contract is locked in the spec.
